doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Luck of the gig, Mongo audition and replacing Tommy Campbell
summary: He happened to be at his aunt's in the Bronx; six months later he got the job after Tommy Campbell left.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That’s terrific. And the first gig with Dizzy, just before you told that story you had said with all the other things, you need a little bit of luck and I think you had it.

Oh yes, oh yes. Could you imagine all the names, the drummer’s names Dizzy Gillespie had in his book? And he started calling people [gap] were busy. I could have been busy that night playing a little gig somewhere. And it happens that I was at my aunt’s apartment in the Bronx doing nothing that day. So it was meant to be. It is luck. I always tell people Dizzy and I would have crossed paths anyway because before joining the Dizzy Gillespie band I had auditioned to be Mongo Santamaria’s drummer. So I would run into Dizzy somewhere at a festival, here, in Europe, somewhere. And you know eventually [gap]. But the way it happened it was too soon, because I played that night, it was just a one night gig. I made a good impression on him obviously because like six months later when his drummer left he called up Mario and he told Mario, I’m looking for a drummer so if the Cuban guy is available tell him that he’s got the gig.
Who was it that you replaced? I’m trying to remember.

I replaced a drummer, a young drummer at that time, Tommy Campbell. Great drummer. He was graduated from Berklee. He was Dizzy’s drummer at that time then Tommy left to go and play with John McLaughlin and Dizzy called me. That’s how I got the gig.
